solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Man's town house? Head for the country no longer

definitions.text: Head for the country no longer

blocks.note: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man
a house is a home

explanation.surface: Someone's town house turns out to be a head of state who has left the country for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Alec Douglas-Home was British Prime Minister in 1963-64, so he is a head of government no longer.
explanation.definitionFit: A former Prime Minister once headed the government of the nation, a role he no longer holds.

clue.text: Brought up fake text for a PC?

indicators.note: in a down clue, something brought up is read from bottom to top, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: cod as an adjective means sham or mock

explanation.surface: Someone has produced a counterfeit document on their computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A doc is the short form of document, the usual file a word processor on a computer produces.

clue.text: Jacket from upmarket clothing pile not fitting

indicators.note: a jacket is the outside covering, so only the outer letters of the next word are taken
clothing something means wrapping round it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of upmarket
nap is the raised pile on cloth such as velvet

explanation.surface: A posh jacket whose pile of fabric does not fit the wearer properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unapt is a rare synonym for unsuitable or inappropriate, the opposite of apt.

clue.text: Worse French ruler putting down one former ruler

indicators.note: putting something down in a down clue lowers it, so it is lifted from its place and set further down

blocks.note: Louis was the name of many French kings
the Roman numeral for one
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A French king fares worse when he deposes one of his predecessors.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'putting down' the one means shifting it lower in the king's name, so it lands just before the former ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Lousy means very bad, so its comparative form means worse in an informal register.

clue.text: Shock about secretary turning on one fired in the office?

indicators.note: turning round means the word for secretary is read backwards
about means surrounding, so the word for shock goes round the rest

blocks.note: to shock is to stun
PA is personal assistant
in cricket, the on side is the leg side

explanation.surface: An office scene where a shocked secretary turns on a colleague who has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests sacking, but a staple gun fires staples. In cricket the on side is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple gun is a tool that shoots staples, used in offices for pinning paper to boards.

clue.text: Oscar for each actor? Just the lead in dramatic work

indicators.note: only the leading character of the following word is kept

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet
per means for each
the first letter of actor

explanation.surface: An Oscar for every actor, though only the lead in the drama gets one.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged work of drama set to music.

clue.text: French miss typical ending for superlative fashion mag

blocks.note: superlatives often end -est, as in biggest
Elle is a fashion magazine

explanation.surface: A young Frenchwoman ends up at the top of a fashion magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Estelle is a French girl's name, and a miss is an unmarried girl or woman.

clue.text: Robert Browning's beginning Ring and Book

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first character, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of Browning
a ring is round like the letter O
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: The start of Robert Browning's long poem The Ring and the Book.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ring and the Book is a long poem by Robert Browning, which makes 'Robert' look like part of the name rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob is the usual pet form of the given name Robert.

clue.text: Receive a royal honour after king's left knowing nothing

indicators.note: having left means having gone away, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: to be knighted is to receive a knighthood from the monarch
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone is knighted once the king has gone, yet remains ignorant.
explanation.definitionFit: Benighted means in intellectual darkness, ignorant or unenlightened.

clue.text: Energy firm keeping trademarks present in group of posters

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the energy firm wraps round the next word

blocks.note: BP is the oil and energy company
logos are brand emblems
present in the sense of being here

explanation.surface: An energy company keeps its trademarks on show, perhaps on billboards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posters' suggests billboards; here they are people who post online.
explanation.definitionFit: The blogosphere is the online community of bloggers, people who post content on the web.

clue.text: Clot got a clue, surprisingly grasping answer

indicators.note: grasping means holding, so the single letter goes inside the other words
something that happens surprisingly comes out in an unexpected way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A dimwit unexpectedly worked out a clue and grabbed the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' reads as an insult for a fool, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To clot is to thicken into a solid mass, which is what blood does when it coagulates.

clue.text: Fictional Amerindian soldiers leaving Canadian city

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so those letters go out of the city name

blocks.note: Toronto is Canada's largest city
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A fictional Native American with soldiers leaving a Canadian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonto is the Native American companion of the Lone Ranger in the radio and TV westerns.

clue.text: Run away from an exhilarating experience in colony

indicators.note: going away from something means leaving it, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written
a thrill is an exciting experience

explanation.surface: Someone flees an exciting experience in a colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run away' reads as fleeing, but it means R is taken out of AN THRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthill is a mound built by an ant colony, and stands for the colony itself.

clue.text: Hear pianola playing, or a wind instrument

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being played about with into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between listening to a player piano or a wind instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aeolian harp is not blown by a player: it is a stringed box sounded by the wind passing over it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aeolian harp, named after Aeolus the Greek god of winds, is played by the wind itself.

clue.text: Completely right to eat for example nothing in fast

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the letter for right swallows the abbreviation

blocks.note: all means completely, as in all alone
R is short for right
e.g. stands for for example
zero, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone who is fasting is told it is quite all right to eat nothing, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as going without food, but it is the musical speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction for a quick, lively tempo.

clue.text: It may make basket cases of reclusive isolates, over from the east

indicators.note: a case is the outside covering, so only the outer letters of each following word are kept
in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the first and last letters of reclusive
the first and last letters of isolates
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Hermits who keep to themselves are treated as basket cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basket cases' looks like one phrase meaning hopeless people; the definition stops at basket, and 'cases' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow whose pliant twigs are woven into baskets and wickerwork.

clue.text: Showing admiration, I really have very little time!

definitions.text: I really have very little time!

blocks.note: first meaning: favourably struck by something

blocks.clueFragment: I really have very little time!
blocks.note: second meaning, split into two words: what a busy person exclaims about being short of time

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as I'M PRESSED, being pressed for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impressed is to feel admiration, while 'I'm pressed' is the busy person's excuse of being hurried.

clue.text: Stop and see changes on journey in March

indicators.note: the letters change places, giving a new order

blocks.note: a go is a turn or trip, as in going somewhere
the two words taken as written, without the joining word

explanation.surface: A traveller halts and looks around on a trip taken during the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is a verb. 'and' is part of the fodder phrase but gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The goose step is a stiff-legged way of marching associated with parading troops.

clue.text: Fine day to get into repeat of Love Island

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so the day letter sits within the rest

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys
D is the abbreviation for day
repeat means the pair from the words for love and island is given a second time

explanation.surface: A nice day out ends up on the TV dating show Love Island, again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeat of' means the pair O KEY is used twice, with D between the two copies. Love Island is a British reality dating show.
explanation.definitionFit: Okey-dokey is a jokey form of okay, said to mean fine or agreed.

clue.text: Current opposition that is limiting politician and party

indicators.note: limiting means setting bounds round something, so the first piece encloses the next

blocks.note: i.e. stands for that is
Member of Parliament
a dance is a party

explanation.surface: The present opposition party is constraining a politician and its own members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current opposition' sounds like today's political opponents, but it is electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: Impedance is the total resistance a circuit offers to alternating electric current.

clue.text: Guys' partners crossing a river in foreign capital

indicators.note: crossing something means spanning across it, so the first word goes round the next ones

blocks.note: from the musical Guys and Dolls
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Men's girlfriends cross a river in a capital city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign capital' looks like a city such as Paris; it means foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: Dollars are the currency of the USA and elsewhere, so funds of a foreign country to a Briton.

clue.text: Insulating layer perhaps seals edges of glasshouse

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last characters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: a pod is a group of seals or whales
the first and last letters of glasshouse

explanation.surface: Insulation for a greenhouse is sealed round its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seals' looks like a verb about closing gaps, but it means the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Podge is body fat, a layer that insulates the body against cold.

clue.text: Offering squash with ice, but not cold

indicators.note: but not means without, so the letter for cold is taken out

blocks.note: to squash is to press
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a fruit squash with ice, though not a cold one.
explanation.walkthrough: Squash is a British fruit cordial, which makes it look like the drink being offered.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressie is an informal British word for a present, a gift or offering.

clue.text: Head of Langley called for houses to get bugged

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first character, so only that is kept
houses means gives a home to, so the following word encloses the letter

blocks.note: the first letter of Langley
something called for is needed

explanation.surface: The CIA chief at Langley called for some houses to be wiretapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Langley, Virginia, is the CIA's headquarters, so 'bugged' looks like surveillance; here it means annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate them, as bugging someone also does.

clue.text: Repeat short, simple song on love

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a ditty is a short simple song
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A short love song to be repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to mean the same again, a repetition of what came before.

clue.text: Time for delivery of French fruit, around 2nd of June

indicators.note: the second of a word is its second character, so only that is kept
around means surrounding, so the French words wrap round that letter

blocks.note: du is French for of the
the second letter of June
a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: A shipment of French fruit is expected to arrive in early June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests a parcel, but the due date is when a baby is expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A due date is the expected day for a birth, or any deadline.

clue.text: The main feature of the first dozen letters on line

blocks.note: A to L are the first twelve letters of the alphabet
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone describes the key element of a document: the first twelve letters on a single line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' means the sea, so the main feature is something found in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring of coral reef in the open ocean, and the main is an old word for the sea.

clue.text: One single Spanish vehicle, moving back, is lost

indicators.note: moving back means one letter shifts from the end round to the front of the word

blocks.note: a means one, a single item
SEAT is a Spanish car maker

explanation.surface: A lone Spanish car reversing is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The T at the end of SEAT moves back to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at sea is an idiom for being confused or bewildered, as if lost.

clue.text: Review things like fashion label worn by son

indicators.note: something worn is carried on the body, so one letter is put in among the rest

blocks.note: to take to someone is to like them
CK is Calvin Klein's label
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A critic reviews items such as a designer label that a young man is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes into the middle of TAKE TO, followed by CK.
explanation.definitionFit: To take stock is to assess or review the situation, like counting a shop's goods.

clue.text: First Labour leader picked up mixed drink

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: Keir Hardie was the first leader of the Labour Party

explanation.surface: The first Labour leader collected a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue also hints at Keir Starmer, the current Labour leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Kir is a cocktail of white wine with blackcurrant liqueur.

clue.text: Fool, maybe, in party doing a pirouette

indicators.note: a pirouette is a spin on the spot, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

explanation.surface: A fool at a party starts spinning about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' looks like a silly person, but it is a fruit dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a dessert of fruit and cream, and pud is British slang for pudding or dessert.

clue.text: Favouring the right time to invest in retailer, one providing accounts

indicators.note: to invest in something is to put money inside it, so those pieces go into the next word

blocks.note: a retailer is a seller
Tories are the UK's right-wing party
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A right-wing investor decides it is time to buy into a retailer whose books are under scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accounts' looks like financial records but means stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller gives accounts, narratives of events real or imagined.
